{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
Our IT guy kept finding 'critical security vulnerabilities' that only he could fix, always right before budget reviews. He was practically indispensable. After he left, the new guy discovered he'd been creating the vulnerabilities himself, then patching them for credit.

CANDIDATE A:
The neighborhood watch captain reported a dramatic increase in suspicious activity—prowlers, attempted break-ins, vandalism. He organized patrols and got the HOA to buy security cameras. When cameras were installed, all activity stopped. Security footage and his later confession showed that he had staged the vandalism and prowler incidents himself.

CANDIDATE B:
The IT consultant found a critical security vulnerability and reported it through proper channels. The external audit confirmed the flaw existed and his patch fixed it. He received recognition for catching a problem that had escaped everyone else.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:11"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve individuals creating problems themselves to appear indispensable by solving them."}
